text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Chancellor Helmut Kohl, at the U.N. environment summit in New York, calls for more protection for the rainforests.
- Docotor jailed for failing to screen blood samples for the HIV virus, causing death of at least one patient.
- Young members of Kohl's conservatives criticise "logjam of reforms" facing government.
- Wolfgang Schaeuble, parliamentary leader of Kohl's Christian Democrats, rejects criticism by industry of government tax reform plans.
- German tobacco industry relaxed about the effects of U.S. compensation deal on Germany.
HANDELSBLATT
- Bertelsmann and Kirch Group join forces with joint ownership of pay-TV station Premiere and common plans to push forward digital television.
- German banks want to make the use of Eurocheques more difficult, according to information received by Handelsblatt, and experts reckon the cheques could disappear altogether.
- Preferred shares in TV group ProSieben Media AG PSMG_p.F cost between 66 and 72 marks.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Opposition Social Democrats (SPD) want to introduce compensation fund for tobacco consumers similar to one set up in the United States.
- A deputy chairman of Bavaria's Christian Social Union (CSU), members of Kohl's coalition, says European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) should go ahead without France if necessary.
- Schaeuble and Bavarian state premier Edmund Stoiber speak out in favour of continuing with Eurofighter jet project.
- Deutsche Telekom expects 17,000 shareholders to attend its first annual meeting in Frankfurt on Wednesday.
DIE WELT
- Education Minister Juergen Ruettgers blast German school texbooks for not paying enough attention to careers and business.
- Results of Denver summit provoke mixed reaction in Germany, with SPD critcising Kohl's performance while the German Chambers of Industry and Trade (DIHT) pronounce themselves satisfied.
